data.title: Mkango Magnetic Materials Limited Announces Filing Of Supplement To MKAR Proxy Statement
data.description:
CALGARY, AB, LONDON, UK, AND VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / November 20, 2026 / Mkango Magnetic Materials Limited (AIM:MKA)(TSX-V:MKA) ("Mkango" or the "Company") announces that Mkango Rare Earths Limited ("MKAR") and Crown PropTech Acquisitions ("CPTK") have filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC") a supplement (the "Supplement") to the proxy statement/prospectus (the "Proxy Statement/Prospectus") forming part of MKAR's registration statement on Form F-4 (the "Form F-4") relating to the proposed business combination between MKAR and CPTK (the "Proposed Business Combination").

The Supplement, which notes a change in MKAR's proposed board of directors, will be mailed to CPTK shareholders in advance of CPTK's shareholder meeting on 25 November 2026. The Supplement is available on EDGAR at the following hyperlink: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2052373/000121390026122438/ea0313066-424b3_mkango.htm, and will be filed under Mkango's profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca.

About Mkango Magnetic Materials Limited

Mkango is listed on the AIM and the TSX-V Stock Exchanges. Mkango's corporate strategy is to become a market leader in the production of recycled rare earth magnets, alloys and oxides, through its interest in Maginito Limited ("Maginito"), which is owned 79.4 percent by Mkango and 20.6 per cent by CoTec Holdings Corp. ("CoTec"), and the Remloy business acquired by its wholly owned German subsidiary, to develop new sustainable sources of neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium and terbium to supply accelerating demand from electric vehicles, wind turbines and other clean energy technologies.

Maginito holds a 100 percent interest in HyProMag Limited and a 90 percent indirect interest in HyProMag GmbH, focused on short loop rare earth magnet recycling and manufacturing in the UK and Germany, respectively, and a 100 per cent interest in Mkango Rare Earths UK Limited ("Mkango UK"), focused on long loop rare earth magnet recycling in the UK via a chemical processing route.

Maginito and CoTec are also expanding Hydrogen Processing of Magnet Scrap ("HPMS") recycling technology into the United States via the 50/50 owned HyProMag USA joint venture company.

Remloy has developed a plant in Bitterfeld, Germany, which recycles end-of-life rare earth magnets via a melting process (medium loop rare earth magnet recycling) to produce neodymium-iron-boron ("NdFeB") alloy powders for the bonded and hot deformed magnet markets, complementary to HyProMag's short loop recycling process, to produce sintered magnets, and to Mkango UK's long loop recycling process, to produce mixed rare earth carbonates and oxides.

Mkango currently owns 100 percent of the advanced stage Songwe Hill rare earths project in Malawi and the proposed Pulawy rare earths separation plant in Poland. On grant of the large-scale mining licence the Government of Malawi may elect to take a free 10 percent interest in the entity holding that licence. Both the Songwe and Pulawy projects have been selected as Strategic Projects under the European Union Critical Raw Materials Act, as has HyProMag GmbH. Songwe has also received Development Funding from the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC), the U.S. Government's development finance institution, securing US$4.6 million in reimbursable funding for Front End Engineering and Design. MKAR has signed a Business Combination Agreement with CPTK, pursuant to which MKAR, which will hold the Songwe Hill and Pulawy projects, is expected to become listed on Nasdaq, subject to the satisfaction or waiver of closing conditions.

For more information, please visit www.mkangomagneticmaterials.com

About Crown PropTech Acquisitions

CPTK is a Cayman Islands exempted company incorporated in 2020 as a special purpose acquisition company for the purpose of effecting a merger, share exchange, asset acquisition, share purchase, reorganization or similar business combination with one or more businesses. For further information, visit www.crownproptech.com.

Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements

This news release contains "forward-looking statements" and "forward-looking information" within the meaning of applicable Canadian securities legislation and other applicable securities laws (together, "forward-looking statements"), including statements concerning the mailing of the Supplement and the CPTK shareholder meeting, and the statements under "About Mkango Magnetic Materials Limited" concerning the Proposed Business Combination and the development of Mkango's projects.

Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by forward-looking statements, and readers should not place undue reliance on them. Factors that could cause such differences include: any delay in mailing the Supplement or adjournment of the CPTK shareholder meeting; failure to complete the Proposed Business Combination on the terms and timetable contemplated, or at all, including failure to obtain required approvals, the level of redemptions by CPTK shareholders and the consequences for Mkango's status on AIM and the TSX Venture Exchange, including under Rule 14 of the AIM Rules for Companies; delays in commissioning HyProMag GmbH's plant; the availability of financing; demand and pricing for rare earths; technical, permitting and regulatory matters; political, fiscal and other risks in Malawi, Poland, Germany, the United Kingdom and the United States; the ability to scale recycling technologies to commercial scale; the availability of scrap supplies; and cost overruns.

The foregoing list is not exhaustive. Readers should also consider the risks described in CPTK's filings with the SEC, Mkango's filings on SEDAR+, and the Proxy Statement/Prospectus. Forward-looking statements are made as of the date of this news release. Except as required by applicable law, Mkango assumes no obligation to update or revise them.

Important Information for Investors and Shareholders

In connection with the Proposed Business Combination, MKAR has filed the Form F-4 with the SEC, which includes the Proxy Statement/Prospectus, being a definitive proxy statement of CPTK and a prospectus of MKAR with respect to the securities to be offered in the Proposed Business Combination. The Form F-4 was declared effective by the SEC on November 4, 2026, and CPTK has mailed the Proxy Statement/Prospectus, and is mailing the Supplement, to its shareholders of record as at October 30, 2026. CPTK urges investors and other interested persons to read the Proxy Statement/Prospectus as supplemented, as well as other documents filed with the SEC, because these documents contain important information about the Proposed Business Combination. Such persons can also read CPTK's filings with the SEC for a description of the security holdings of its officers and directors and their respective interests as security holders in the consummation of the transactions described herein. The Proxy Statement/Prospectus as supplemented can be obtained, without charge, at www.sec.gov and under Mkango's profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca. In addition, the documents filed by CPTK may be obtained free of charge by directing a request to CPTK c/o Michael Minnick, Chief Executive Officer, 40 West 57th Street, 29th Floor, New York, NY 10019, or by telephone at (212) 796-4796.

Participants in the Solicitation

Investors and security holders may obtain more detailed information regarding the names, affiliations and interests of CPTK's directors and officers in CPTK's SEC filings. data.title: Chattanooga Quantum Collaborative, The Company Lab, and Outset Ventures Join Forces to Accelerate Quantum Commercialization
data.description:
Chattanooga Quantum Collaborative, The Company Lab, and Outset Ventures Join Forces to Accelerate Quantum Commercialization

The partnership combines Tennessee's quantum ecosystem, commercialization expertise and international venture capital to bring quantum innovation to market faster

The Chattanooga Quantum Collaborative (CQC), The Company Lab (CO.LAB), and New Zealand-based Outset Ventures are combining their strengths to accelerate quantum commercialization, moving quantum innovation from the lab into the hands of the people and industries that can use it.

A memorandum of understanding between the three organizations establishes an international partnership to streamline commercialization, open paths to enterprise customers, and mobilize investment capital. Each organization fulfills a distinct role in the commercialization pathway: CQC leads regional quantum ecosystem development, driving alignment across Tennessee’s research institutions, public-sector assets, and broader economic initiatives. CO.LAB serves as the startup commercialization engine through CO.LAB Q, connecting founders directly with targeted programming, quantum infrastructure providers, corporate pilot opportunities, and enterprise customers across key regional industries. Outset Ventures brings extensive experience backing frontier science, pairing venture capital investment with active deep tech operational support.

“Chattanooga provides the physical infrastructure and testbed capabilities that quantum innovators need to prove their concepts,” said Charlie Brock, CEO of the Chattanooga Quantum Collaborative. “This partnership connects those technical assets directly with commercial opportunities and expanded investment—including joint investment pathways. Tying market access to institutional capital accelerates how quickly these innovations transform from technical promise into market-ready ventures.”

Opportunities enter the partnership through any of the three organizations, triggering a tailored mix of support designed around each startup’s specific needs—ranging from technical validation on real-world testbeds to customer introductions, pilot deployment, and co-investment capital.

“Quantum founders face a unique set of challenges that require specialized infrastructure, real enterprise customers, and investors who truly understand deep tech,” said Tasia Malakasis, CEO of The Company Lab. “Through CO.LAB Q—our dedicated quantum studio—and our partners at Outset and CQC, we can now provide them with direct access to all of those critical enablers.”

The partnership names Chattanooga and Tennessee as a key U.S. market entry hub for ventures across the partners’ international networks. For global founders, the agreement provides a direct landing pad to test technologies on commercial quantum infrastructure and access North American enterprise customers. For Tennessee companies, it creates direct pathways to international capital markets and foreign expansion.

Outset Ventures brings a proven track record of scaling frontier science. Headquartered in Auckland, New Zealand, Outset provides deep tech startups with venture funding, incubation, and specialized laboratory infrastructure—having served as the early home to breakthrough companies like Rocket Lab, LanzaTech, and Mint Innovation. The firm recently closed a NZ$41.5 million fund dedicated to early-stage science and engineering startups.

“Deep tech companies from small markets have to go global early, and the United States is usually the first stop,” said Mat Rowe, Executive Director and Partner at Outset Ventures. “Chattanooga gives our portfolio founders a place where they can test on real infrastructure, connect with enterprise customers, and engage with capital and partners who already understand quantum.”

Isay Acenas, Principal Investor at Outset Ventures and a key driver behind this international partnership, said, “The science is moving quickly. The harder question is how quickly it becomes a product someone buys. This partnership is built around that question, with each of us contributing a critical piece of the pathway.”

Chattanooga is home to the EPB Quantum Center, the nation’s first commercial hub offering quantum networking and quantum computing under one roof. The city is also home to the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga’s Quantum Center, where more than 25 researchers work across quantum networking, sensing, algorithms and control, and to the Institute for Quantum Innovation, a new research and graduate education center from Vanderbilt University and EPB.

Nearby, Oak Ridge National Laboratory hosts the Department of Energy’s Quantum Science Center, and the state’s $43 million Tennessee Quantum Initiative is investing in quantum infrastructure across Tennessee.

Parties interested in working with the partnership can contact info@chattanoogaquantum.com.

About the Chattanooga Quantum Collaborative

The Chattanooga Quantum Collaborative (CQC) is a nonprofit organization working to establish the Chattanooga and Tennessee region as a nationally recognized, thriving quantum cluster that drives long-term regional economic prosperity. CQC mobilizes regional partners to grow the quantum ecosystem, prepare talent at every level, and help local industry explore and adopt quantum technologies. Learn more at www.ChattanoogaQuantum.com.

About The Company Lab (CO.LAB)

The Company Lab (CO.LAB) is a place-based entrepreneurial support organization accelerating startups in Chattanooga’s industries of strength: energy, mobility, and quantum. By connecting founders with the region’s world-class infrastructure, real-world testbeds, industry expertise, capital, and corporate partners, CO.LAB helps startups validate and scale emerging technologies while advancing corporate innovation priorities. Through this work, CO.LAB strengthens the regional economy and positions Chattanooga as a national hub for commercializing the technologies shaping our future. Learn more at www.thecompanylab.org.

About Outset Ventures

Outset Ventures is a deep technology incubator and early-stage investor based in Parnell, Auckland. Its campus, Future House, is a multistorey research and development facility that is home to more than 20 deep tech companies, a mix of Outset portfolio companies and independent residents. Facility alumni include Rocket Lab, LanzaTech and Mint Innovation, and founders of those companies sit on Outset’s investment committee. Learn more at outset.ventures.

Media Contact: Danna Bailey | Danna@ChattanoogaQuantum.com | 423-802-9549

data.title: YPTC Brings Nonprofit Accounting and Fractional CFO Services to Florida
data.description:
YPTC Brings Nonprofit Accounting and Fractional CFO Services to Florida

YPTC Brings Nonprofit Accounting and Fractional CFO Services to Florida

PR Newswire

JACKSONVILLE, Fla., Nov. 20, 2026

JACKSONVILLE, Fla., Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Your Part-Time Controller, LLC (YPTC), a leading provider of nonprofit accounting and fractional CFO services, is proud to announce its regional office expansion to Florida. This YPTC office will be based in Jacksonville and serve the entire state. 

Florida is already a key location for YPTC, with a strong base of clients and team members across the state. With a dedicated presence, YPTC will build on that foundation and create stronger connections across Jacksonville, Tallahassee, Tampa Bay, Orlando, Miami, and the communities in between.

The Jacksonville-based office is YPTC's sixteenth office opening, reflecting the firm's growth and investment in the southeast region and continued commitment to serving Florida's nonprofit sector.

YPTC's Florida Office Director Lisa Dries says, "For me, it's about building on the relationships we already have across Florida, growing our connections within the nonprofit community, and bringing YPTC's nonprofit financial expertise to more organizations. We want to be the trusted local partner that helps nonprofits build a strong financial foundation so they can stay focused on what matters most: their missions."

YPTC has been serving clients in Florida since 2022. Lisa is proud of the impacts the firm has already made for Florida nonprofits, the support being provided, and the continued commitment reflected in this office opening. She is excited to connect with even more nonprofit leaders, deepen YPTC's involvement in communities across the state, and continue building a Florida team that can grow alongside the organizations YPTC serves. 

The experienced professionals at YPTC deliver flexible, specialized nonprofit accounting and fractional CFO services. Their support gives nonprofit leaders the financial clarity and strategic insight they need while allowing them to stay focused on their missions.

To learn more about Your Part-Time Controller, LLC visit yptc.com. 

About Lisa Dries

Lisa Dries is Director of YPTC's Florida Region. Since joining the firm in 2022, Lisa has supported nonprofit organizations throughout Florida while helping grow and develop YPTC's local team. She is passionate about building strong relationships, bringing people together to solve challenges, and helping nonprofit leaders gain the financial clarity and confidence they need to advance their missions.

Lisa is a licensed CPA in Pennsylvania with more than 20 years of experience in auditing, accounting, and financial leadership across nonprofit and for-profit sectors. She works alongside a talented team of professionals committed to serving nonprofits and helping organizations thrive.

About YPTC

YOUR PART-TIME CONTROLLER, LLC (YPTC) is a national accounting firm with over thirty years of experience building stronger nonprofits. YPTC offers specialized nonprofit accounting services, including fractional/outsourced CFO, accounting and month-end financial management, financial planning and analysis, and grant management and compliance. Support, flexibility, and transformation mark our overall approach; we meet clients wherever they are. As a trusted thought partner, YPTC allows nonprofits to focus on what matters: furthering the mission of the organization. For more information, please visit our website www.yptc.com.

data.title: EU Open to 'Closest Possible Relationship' With U.K., Chief Says — Update
data.description:
By Edith Hancock

The European Union is open to having a much closer relationship with the U.K., the head of the European Council said, as both sides continue work to thaw ties more than a decade after Britain voted to leave the bloc.

"We remain open to [having] the closest possible relationship between the European Union and the United Kingdom," European Council President Antonio Costa said Friday in Brussels.

U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham was in the Belgian capital for a U.K.-EU summit to strike agreements on issues including youth mobility and food exports.

The EU's Costa said Europe would respect whatever decision the U.K. takes about its future ties with the bloc.

"Europe needs unity," he said, adding the European Union will always seek to work closely with the U.K.

The U.K. and EU struck deals on three key areas: linking the EU and the U.K.'s emissions trading systems, a visa program that would allow young people more flexibility to live and work either side of the English Channel, and reducing border frictions for food and animal products.

"This is a good day for Britain, and this is a good day for Europe," Burnham told reporters, adding the deal directly addresses the biggest worries the public has such as food prices.

data.title: Qualified Upgrades Its ZoomInfo Integration to the GTM.AI API, Bringing Verified Company and Contact Data to Piper
data.description:
Qualified Upgrades Its ZoomInfo Integration to the GTM.AI API, Bringing Verified Company and Contact Data to Piper

ZoomInfo (NASDAQ: GTM), the all-in-one AI GTM platform, today announced that Qualified from Salesforce has upgraded its ZoomInfo integration to the ZoomInfo GTM.AI API. Qualified now enriches website visitor profiles through the API's company and contact enrichment endpoints, replacing the legacy WebSights and Enterprise APIs, so Piper, Qualified's agent, works from verified ZoomInfo company and contact data.

For Qualified customers, the integration works as it did before. They connect their ZoomInfo account in Qualified, and visitor profiles are enriched automatically, with no change to their setup.

The integration enriches each website visitor at two points. When a visitor arrives on a customer's website, Qualified uses reverse IP enrichment to add ZoomInfo company data to the visitor's profile. When a visitor shares an email address, Qualified uses email enrichment to add ZoomInfo contact data.

Both enrichment steps run automatically, at the same two points every time. The data flows into Qualified visitor fields, the context Qualified holds on each website visitor. Customers choose which fields Piper can use in conversations and which fields drive deterministic workflows such as segmentation and routing.

The API gives partners and customers programmatic access to ZoomInfo's verified company and contact data. The Qualified integration uses two of its endpoints, company enrichment and contact enrichment, and only the fields those endpoints return.

Customers connect the integration with their existing ZoomInfo account.

“Qualified customers already generate pipeline with Piper,” said Dennis Sevilla, Chief Strategy Officer at ZoomInfo. “ZoomInfo adds verified company and contact data to every visitor profile. Piper starts each conversation knowing more about who she is talking to, and teams can segment and route visitors on data they trust.”

Qualified customers can connect ZoomInfo from the Qualified settings page at app.qualified.com/settings/zoominfo. Customers who do not see the option can contact their Qualified Success Architect (QSA). Details are also available on the ZoomInfo integrations page at zoominfo.com/integrations/qualified.

The upgrade puts Qualified on the same GTM.AI API that ZoomInfo partners use to bring verified company and contact data into their platforms.

About ZoomInfo

ZoomInfo (NASDAQ: GTM), the all-in-one AI GTM platform, enables sales, marketing, and customer success teams to execute their go-to-market strategy with confidence. Powered by the industry's most comprehensive B2B data, including more than 100 million companies, 500 million contacts, and billions of signals, ZoomInfo delivers the intelligence, automation, and integrations that modern revenue teams need to identify, engage, and convert their best buyers.

GTM.AI is a headless layer that connects to ZoomInfo's GTM Context Graph. It is the API and Model Context Protocol home for AI agents, powering integrations across Salesforce, HubSpot, Microsoft, Anthropic, OpenAI, Perplexity, and dozens more.

Learn more at zoominfo.com and gtm.ai.

data.title: ILLRW Lawsuit: Robbins LLP Reminds Triller Group, Inc. Investors to Contact the Firm About the Opportunity to Lead the Class Action Lawsuit
data.description:
ILLRW Lawsuit: Robbins LLP Reminds Triller Group, Inc. Investors to Contact the Firm About the Opportunity to Lead the Class Action Lawsuit

ILLRW Lawsuit: Robbins LLP Reminds Triller Group, Inc. Investors to Contact the Firm About the Opportunity to Lead the Class Action Lawsuit

PR Newswire

SAN DIEGO, Nov. 20, 2026

SAN DIEGO, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Shareholder rights law firm Robbins LLP reminds investors that a class action was filed on behalf of all persons who purchased Triller Group Inc. (NASDAQ: ILLRW) securities between October 16, 2024 and December 29, 2025, inclusive (the "Class Period"). Triller was formerly known as AGBA Group Holding Limited ("AGBA").

The complaint alleges that Triller failed to disclose that it would be unable to timely file required financial reports with the SEC.

Investors who purchased Triller Group Inc. securities during the Class Period and suffered significant losses should contact Robbins LLP for information about the lawsuit and the December 14, 2026 lead plaintiff motion deadline.

Why Was Triller Sued?

According to the complaint, on October 15, 2024, AGBA completed a merger (the "Merger") between itself and, inter alia, Triller Corp. ("Legacy Triller"), a Delaware corporation that operated as a purported next generation, artificial intelligence-("AI") powered, social media and live-streaming event platform for creators. As a result of the Merger, Legacy Triller became a wholly owned subsidiary of AGBA, AGBA changed its name to "Triller Group Inc.", and the combined Company purportedly began operating both AGBA's and Legacy Triller's respective businesses.

The complaint alleges that leading up to and following the Merger, the Company touted the various Legacy Triller assets purportedly acquired in the Merger, including, Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship ("BKFC"), which stages live and streamed combat sports events, and which the Company touted as "the fastest-growing combat league in the industry."

Plaintiff contends that during the Class Period, defendants failed to disclose that:

(i) Triller's control over and consolidation of BKFC was tenuous, overstated, and/or non-existent;

(ii) Triller could not timely file one or more of its periodic financial reports with the SEC as required by the Nasdaq's listing requirements, in part, because of accounting issues related to the foregoing;

(iii) as a result of all the foregoing, Triller was at an increased risk of being delisted from the Nasdaq;

(iv) accordingly, Triller's disclosure controls and procedures were deficient, the full scope and severity of issues with its financial controls were understated, and the overall benefits of the Merger were overstated;

(v) defendants likewise overstated Triller's ability to address its non-compliance with the Nasdaq's listing requirements; and

(vi) as a result, defendants' public statements were materially false and misleading at all relevant times.

Why Did Triller Stock Drop?

Several disclosures between March 31, 2025 and December 30, 2025, regarding Triller's inability to file its annual report with the SEC, were followed by Triller's stock decline. According to the complaint, on December 30, 2025, Triller issued a press release announcing its receipt of "a determination letter from a Nasdaq Hearings Panel on December 26, 2025, confirming the suspension of trading on the Nasdaq Stock Market effective at the open of the market on December 30, 2025 and delisting of the Company's securities", "stem[ming] from the Company not having been able to file two periodic reports by a deadline of December 24, 2025 set by the Hearings Panel." The press release further disclosed that "[t]he filing delay is attributable primarily to one remaining technical matter involving the consolidation of accounts for a U.S.-based operation within Triller Group"—not yet disclosed to be BKFC. On this news, Triller's stock price fell $3.38 per share, or 91.35%, over the following two trading sessions, to close at $0.32 per share on December 31, 2025.

Triller's securities were suspended from trading from December 30, 2025 to April 15, 2026. Triller most recently received a notice of non-compliance from the NASDAQ Staff on September 2, 2026, and, as of the time of the filing of this Complaint, its common stock trades for pennies.

Listen to Our Podcast

What Can Triller Shareholders Do Now?

Investors who purchased Triller Group Inc. securities during the Class Period may be eligible to serve as lead plaintiff. The lead plaintiff is a court-appointed investor who represents the interests of all class members throughout the litigation. Stockholders who wish to seek appointment as lead plaintiff must move the court no later than December 14, 2026. Contact Robbins LLP for information about the appointment process.

Shareholders do not need to serve as lead plaintiff to share in any potential recovery. Investors who do not seek appointment may remain absent class members.

Does It Cost Anything to Participate?

No. Robbins LLP represents investors on a contingency fee basis, with no upfront or out-of-pocket fees or expenses.

Contact Robbins LLP

Investors seeking additional information about the Triller Group Inc. securities class action may contact Robbins LLP by submitting an inquiry, emailing attorney Aaron Dumas, Jr., or calling (800) 350-6003.

Why Robbins LLP?

A recognized leader in shareholder rights litigation, Robbins LLP represents investors in securities fraud and shareholder derivative litigation. We have helped restore more than $2 billion in value to shareholders and secured some of the largest recoveries in shareholder derivative litigation history. 

"Companies have an obligation to provide investors with complete and accurate information so that markets can function fairly and efficiently," said Brian J. Robbins, Founding Partner of Robbins LLP.

To be notified if a class action against Triller Group Inc. settles, or to receive free alerts when corporate executives engage in wrongdoing, sign up for Stock Watch today.

data.title: Anthropic's stock slides closer to IPO price and drags down the AI trade
data.description:
By Emily Bary

Anthropic's inability to hold its opening stock price has been seen as 'bad for the rest of tech'

Anthropic finished with a $1.29 trillion valuation on Thursday.

There was no honeymoon period for Anthropic after its record-breaking initial public offering.

Shares of the AI company are down more than 9% in morning action on Friday, making for a gloomy second day of trading. Anthropic's stock (ANT) is at $88.16, well below its $111.50 opening price, and falling closer to its $83 IPO price.

It's a downbeat sign for the broader technology ecosystem as well, with AI stocks taking a beating across the board. Among notable losers are shares of Sandisk (SNDK), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Dell Technologies (DELL), Nebius Group (NBIS) and Arm Holdings (ARM).

"The vast majority of this continued selling pressure in the last 24 hours feels more to do with" the Anthropic IPO than it does with some less-than-perfect earnings reports in the technology sector, according to Jefferies trading-desk analyst Jeffrey Favuzza.

He wrote in a note to clients that Anthropic's inability to hold its opening price and the downward pressure in Friday's premarket action is being viewed as "bad for the rest of tech."

Anthropic's IPO was seen as a tentpole event for the AI trade. The company finished with a $1.29 trillion valuation on Thursday, according to Dow Jones Market Data. Friday's action brings that down to $1.16 trillion.

"Anthropic's strong debut alongside a falling technology sector suggests investors still believe in AI but are becoming more selective about what they will pay for that growth," David Miller, the chief investment officer at Catalyst Funds, said in emailed comments.

Some analysts initiated coverage of Anthropic's stock after Thursday's close, chiming in with mixed views.

Don't miss: After Anthropic's 'bittersweet' IPO, here's what lies ahead

"We are cautious, not negative," wrote Seaport Research's Jay Goldberg, who launched coverage of shares with a neutral rating.

He called Anthropic an "incredible company," but also one "asking for an incredible leap of faith by investors."

"We think the company will need time to grow into its valuation and answer some very big questions about its growth trajectory," he continued. For instance, the company saw 43% revenue growth from the second quarter to the third quarter. That compared with a much faster 144% growth rate from the first quarter to the second quarter.

Goldberg referred to that as a "worrying" deceleration. "To merit its valuation, it will need to see much higher growth rates over the next two years," he added.

William Blair's Arjun Bhatia was more upbeat, calling Anthropic a "generational company driving a generational technology shift" as he began his own coverage of the stock with an outperform rating.

"Questions about the future are worth asking, even those that don't have an answer at this point," he wrote.

But at the same time, he and his team "don't want to miss the forest for the trees."

"We think AI is a generational shift in the tech landscape, and Anthropic is leading the charge in developing AI with a select handful of other companies," Bhatia wrote. "Over the next decade, we think Anthropic is only going to become more important and consume a greater portion of enterprise spend," meaning it will command more of the budget that businesses have to allocate toward technology.

See also: Anthropic soared in its debut as stocks tanked. Only one other IPO has done that since 1990.

-Emily Bary

data.title: ICE Canada Morning Comment: ICE Canola Futures Softer
data.description:
WINNIPEG, Manitoba--ICE canola futures were posting small losses Friday morning as values continued to chop around in narrow, rangebound trade.

The January contract was down $2.50 at C$774.50 per tonne in early activity.

Overnight losses in Chicago soyoil, European rapeseed and Malaysian palm oil accounted for some spillover selling pressure.

Canada exported 141,000 tonnes of canola during the week ended Nov. 15, which was roughly half of what moved the previous week, reported the Canadian Grain Commission.

However, marketing-year-to-date exports of 2.66 million tonnes remain well ahead of the 1.83 million tonnes exported by the same point in 2025-26.

Updated supply/demand estimates from Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada included only minor adjustments to the canola balance sheet, with projected 2026-27 ending stocks lowered to 1.87 million tonnes from 1.97 million in October.

Projected exports for the year were left unchanged at 7.7 million tonnes, while domestic usage was raised by 100,000 tonnes to 14.5 million.

About 14,300 canola contracts had traded as of 8:46 a.m. ET.

data.title: I'm terrified of a market crash. Should I put $400,000 of my $1 million retirement savings into an annuity?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

'We have a house worth $450,000. Our combined annual income is $125,000.'

"We don't have any nonqualified brokerage investments, and our combined annual income is $125,000." (Photo subjects are models.)

Dear Quentin,

I'm wondering what your thoughts are on putting our house and other assets into a trust. Could it help reduce taxes or protect our assets from lawsuits, bankruptcy or other unforeseen circumstances? If so, what are the potential downsides or pitfalls?

We have a house worth $450,000 and about $1 million in retirement assets held in various qualified accounts. I'd also be interested in your thoughts on annuities for capital preservation and guaranteed income.

Would it make sense to put $400,000 of our $1 million in qualified retirement accounts into an annuity that would begin paying out at age 65, guaranteeing us $40,000 a year for life, while leaving the remaining $600,000 invested in a brokerage account for capital appreciation?

My spouse and I are 55 and 54, respectively. We're both working and plan to continue until 65. We're terrified of a market crash. We don't have any nonqualified brokerage investments, and our combined annual income is $125,000.

Curious in the Midwest

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: 'Nvidia has me spooked ': Should I sell my stocks or buy real estate?

That money you invest in an annuity is no longer readily available, and you give up any stock-market gains it might have earned.

Dear Curious,

I'll outline the advantages of your proposal - and then move on to the cons.

First, the pros of putting your money in an annuity, I presume, are to find a haven for part of your nest egg, albeit at a potentially lower rate than the stock market could provide. If you moved $400,000 from traditional 401(k)s or IRAs into an IRA annuity, the transaction generally would not trigger income taxes or the 10% early-withdrawal penalty, provided the funds are transferred correctly. A direct trustee-to-trustee transfer is typically the simplest approach. If you were selling $400,000 worth of investments in an ordinary brokerage account, however, you could owe capital-gains taxes on any profits realized from the sale.

Annuities provide guaranteed income, much like Social Security, which you presumably plan to take when you reach full retirement age. What you receive depends on the type of annuity: your initial investment, the interest rate or other terms you lock in and, of course, the payment schedule. Payouts can also vary with your age, your sex and whether the product is a joint-life annuity. If you expect to live a long time, a lifetime annuity can protect you from outliving your retirement savings. The trade-off is access: That money is no longer readily available, and you give up any stock-market gains it might have earned.

Annuities provide guaranteed income, much like Social Security.

An annuity is neither a bond nor cash. It works as an insurance contract: you pay an insurance company in exchange for income. An immediate annuity starts paying within a year of purchase, while a deferred annuity starts at a later date. Money in a 401(k) or IRA that is invested in stocks can grow over time and help keep pace with inflation. Annuity income is usually fixed, so it can lose purchasing power as prices rise unless you add an inflation adjustment or rider, but that protection also comes at a price: a lower initial payout. Annuity fees can be as much as 10% of the value of your contract. Surrender charges can be substantial if you withdraw money early.

But I have some questions: I understand why the prospect of $40,000 in guaranteed annual income is tempting. If payments continued for those periods, you would collect $400,000 over 10 years, $800,000 over 20 years and potentially $1.2 million over 30 years. Make sure you read the fine print. Is that $40,000 guaranteed income for one person's lifetime? Or is it for both of your lifetimes? Does the surviving spouse continue to receive the full $40,000-a-year income? Is there a death benefit or return-of-premium provision or rider if one spouse dies? Last but not least, are the $40,000-a-year payments adjusted for inflation?

Don't miss: My wife and I are in our 70s. Should we pay off our 2.5% mortgage or invest in a stock market driven by AI?

Investing in the stock market

Third, the pros of leaving the money in the stock market: If you left your $400,000 invested for another 10 years instead of putting it into an annuity, it could grow to approximately $592,000 at an annual return of 4%, $787,000 at 7%, or $864,000 at 8%. These estimates assume annual compounding, with investment earnings reinvested, and exclude taxes, fees and additional contributions. The biggest difference between this scenario and the option of buying an annuity with your $400,000 is that the former is not guaranteed. You are potentially giving up the prospect of a larger return in exchange for security.

An annuity and a trust provide different estate-planning functions. Annuities distribute your assets per the terms of the contract, whereas a trust is designed to manage, protect and distribute your estate during your lifetime and beyond. As this guide on Estate Guru points out, trusts and annuities solve different estate-planning problems: (1) Bypassing probate or buying an annuity isn't an estate plan. (2) A trust can manage your assets if you become incapacitated, provide for minor children or beneficiaries with special needs, address the complications of a blended family and set out the conditions for an inheritance.

Revocable living trusts can benefit people with modest estates, particularly those seeking to avoid probate or plan for incapacity. For families with complicated estates, putting accounts and assets under a single trustee can keep everything running smoothly. It can also help prevent conflicts involving beneficiary designations. Marital trusts matter most in blended families, where each spouse wants to be sure their own children are provided for if the other dies. A special-needs trust can supplement government benefits, while a spendthrift trust can prevent beneficiaries from selling or using their future inheritance as collateral for a loan.

Know what you're buying, and be sure you're doing it for the right reasons.

Related: Is Social Security a Ponzi scheme? No. Don't get carried away with 1930s-era prophecies of doom.
